text:
Adin Hill gave Vegas the night. Buffalo outshot the Golden Knights 29 to 26 on goal and had 78 shot attempts to their 51, but Hill stopped 28 of 29. By our numbers he saved 2.3 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved (that's goals saved above expected, how many more pucks a goalie stops than an average one would on the same chances). Hill was drafted 76th overall by the Coyotes in 2015, and he looked like a first-rounder here. VGK beat BUF 4-1 at KeyBank Center and have won three straight.

Buffalo owned the first period, out-chancing Vegas 1.49 to 0.51 in expected goals, which measures the quality of chances rather than the count. The Sabres had nothing to show for it. Mitch Marner broke the game open in the second with a shorthanded wrist shot at 12:17, and Jack Eichel made it 2-0 just 86 seconds later. Beck Malenstyn pulled BUF within one early in the third, but Tomas Hertl answered 77 seconds later and added another at the 10:00 mark. Hertl's second came off a look worth only 8 percent, the kind of goal a goalie has every right to expect to stop.

Over the whole game, the numbers call it close. Our simulation of every shot gives VGK 52 percent to win and BUF 48, so the 4-1 final overstates the gap in play. Colten Ellis allowed four on 26 shots, about half a goal worse than expected, while Hill covered for a team that spent long stretches chasing the puck. Vegas has won three in a row. The Sabres will wonder how a game they controlled early got away from them.
